**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (a `feat`, so it merges at the next cut, after its parent #560 / #551, which is under its own review).

Scope: only this PR's own commits (023324e0, fc7ab7c9, cded9490 = `13a12a25 ^f5d8c06a ^origin/main`), trial-merged with `origin/main` a0891091. The merge was clean. No snapshot PNG, process file, build.rs, `.github` or dependency change is among this PR's own commits.

### What looks good
- **Side does not depend on winding.** `Region::new` orients by nesting parity, and the offset sign comes from the stated side alone (`ring.rs:81`). A CW and a CCW copy of the same profile give identical paths for both die and punch.
- **Kerf certificate** (`laws::kerf`). Every move, leads included, is held at least the offset (less 10 nm) from the profile. A lead that crossed the profile would be refused, not trimmed.
- **Neck and notch topology is caught after the offset.** A die whose offset splits into two loops is refused as a "neck". A punch whose outward offset closes a mouth into a hole is refused as a "slot". The multiplicity check runs on the offset, not only on the input.
- **One post door.** The post refusal sits in `op_streams` (`posting.rs:828`), and `post_setup`, `posting_mounts` and `posting_per_op` all go through it. The family door at post (`admits`) also refuses a wire op that ends up on a non-EDM machine.
- **Command doors.** `tool_door`, `wire_gate` and `family_gate` run on Create, Paste, Edit, ChangeKind and EditLinks. A wire op naming a tool, a mill op on a wire EDM, and a wire op on a mill are all refused at creation. A missing condition, gap or wire diameter is refused by name.
- **Stale stamp.** It digests the condition's id, wire and gap (`stamp_condition`) plus side, start and planes (`params.rs`). Editing the machine's table marks the op stale.
- **Shared match sites.** Every match that handles `PlasmaProfile` also handles `WireContour` explicitly. I found no wildcard arm that treats it as a mill contour.
- **Code law.** No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside tests. Float-to-int casts are clamped. New files are under 250 lines and carry provenance lines (general practice plus #290's decisions).

### Local results (merged with main a0891091)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib wire` | 5 passed |
| app `--test wire_contour` | 7 passed |
| app `--test golden_cl` | 26 passed |
| app `--test operations` | 117 passed, 6 ignored |
| app `--test edm_machine` / `edm_conditions` | 7 / 6 passed |
| app `--test project_roundtrip` | 71 passed |
| app `--test tool_gate` / `tool_law` / `ribbon` | 9 / 4 / 12 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` | 121 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 538 passed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Goldens checked by hand.** Profile 40x20 with r2 corners, k = 0.125 + 0.04 = 0.165:
- `wire_contour_die.cl` runs at y = -9.835 (inside) with a corner radius of 1.835.
- `wire_contour_punch.cl` runs at x = -20.165 (outside) with a corner radius of 2.165.

### Attacks tried
I ran throwaway local probes against `wire_contour`; nothing was committed. Every attack held:
- **Fillets at the corner minimum** (die, 1-degree facets):
  - r = k+1 um and r = k are cut. At r = k the closest approach is 3 nm under k, inside `PATH_TOL`.
  - r = k-1 um and r = k-3 um are **cut with a sharp mitred corner**, leaving at most (sqrt2 - 1)(k - r) ≈ 1.2 um of material in the corner.
  - r = k-5 um and r = k-10 um are refused by name.
- **Dead-end slot off a die opening:** 2k+4 um and 2k+1 um are cut. 2k, 2k-1 um and 2k-3 um are refused ("3.0000 mm standing").
- **Die dumbbell neck:** 2k+2 um and 2k+0.1 um are cut. 2k-0.1 um and 2k-2 um are refused as a "neck". The multiplicity appears only after offsetting, and it is caught.
- **Punch U whose mouth closes after the offset:** refused. A sharp 0.9-degree punch spike is cut, with the mitre squared at x = 60.165.
- **Start hole:**
  - Die: a start outside, on the profile, 0.1 inside, exactly on the path, or 1 um inside the path is refused, each by its own name.
  - Punch: a start inside or 0.1 outside is refused.
  - A C-shaped die with the start in the C's mouth, which is outside the opening, is refused.
  - Valid starts in either arm or the spine of the C give paths with every point inside the opening and the kerf never under k.
- **Path shape:** every accepted path is closed (first == last), has no zero-length moves, and holds Feed moves only. There are no rapids for anything downstream to read as a mill rapid. The lead-out retraces the lead-in, and the notes say so.
- **Degenerate input:** two loops, a bowtie, and a profile at 1e9 mm behave as they should (the first two are refused by name; the far profile is cut with the right offset). A near-collinear vertex plus a 1e-7 mm edge on a punch gives a clean path.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. **The 2 um corner tolerance is silent.** `COVER_TOL` lets a fillet up to about 4.8 um under the minimum be cut with a sharp mitred path corner. The leftover material (at most 2 um) is on the recuttable side for both die and punch, so nothing is gouged. But the drawn radius is not met and nothing in the notes says so. Consider naming it in the path notes, or a smaller tolerance, when the wire verdicts land (#534).
2. **Chord error is not charged to a safe side.** The generator takes the polyline as truth. Chords with their vertices on the true arc:
   - A **punch's convex rounds**: the chord sits inside the true arc, so the kerf eats into the true punch by the sag. This is the scrap side.
   - A **die's convex rounds**: the opening comes out smaller by the sag. This is the safe side.
   - **Concave rounds**: the error falls into the waste, which is safe.

   This is the same property every mill contour has, set by the import's chord cap (#689). Wire EDM tolerances are tighter, though, so a follow-up to bound or report the sag for the wire (or to offset punch rounds by the sag) seems worth filing.
3. **The whole-model source** uses `slice::project` (a union of sampled Z slices). A non-prismatic part loses features that fall between samples. On a punch that would be cut into, so the picked-profile source is the safe one until #534 verifies the sweep.
4. **Which frame is the start hole in?** It is read in the same frame as the picked loops (world XY). If a user types the drilled hole's coordinates in the setup's WCS, and the WCS origin is not the world origin, the lead starts at a different (still waste-side, still kerf-checked) point. The page calls the fields plain "Start hole X/Y". Worth stating the frame on the page when #535 adds the viewport pick.
5. **Posting refuses document-wide.** Any wire op in the document blocks every post, including per-setup and per-mount posting of an unrelated mill setup, until the wire op is suppressed. It is conservative and named, and it ends with #533.
6. **Empty tool, outside the three display sites #1110 lists:**
   - `fixture_struck` returns no findings when the tool is missing.
   - `rest::ahead` books the wire op as a radius-0 cutter. That under-reports removal, which is the conservative side.
   - `stock_sim` refuses the program by name.

   None of these is on a path that can post a wire cut today. #533/#534 should revisit them.
7. **No UI test drives the wire page's fields** (side combo, start hole, condition through Apply). Only the ribbon tip and tab law changed in the UI tests. That is acceptable for a minimal page; it would be good to cover with #535.

Not exercised: an end-to-end app run with a mirrored or rotated part (covered at the generator level by the winding probe), MCP (#1108), and the GUI.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
